meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · AI/ML · solo · run 1
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 2 of 4 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN with 50-epoch one-cycle schedule beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference
artifacts.reason: rejected: test refers to files never uploaded (use the code blob id from lab exec or lab put): }

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 50 epochs with crop/flip augmentation, label smoothing and a one-cycle schedule, using flip test-time augmentation, achieves below 6% test error on CIFAR-10 when trained on all 50k training images.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN with 50-epoch one-cycle schedule beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0095, 95% CI [-0.0137, -0.0053], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 50 epochs with crop/flip augmentation, label smoothing and a one-cycle schedule, with flip test-time augmentation, reaches 5.32% error on a 5k held-out split of the CIFAR-10 training set when trained on 45k images, below the 6% reference; the same recipe trained on all 50k images is used for the test predictions.

artifacts.title: Word+char TF-IDF LinearSVC (C=1) beats TF-IDF+logistic-regression on AG News
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0057, 95% CI [-0.0097, -0.0017], needed below -0.0017

claim.statement: A LinearSVC with C=1.0 on word 1-2gram plus char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF features, trained on all 40k AG News training articles, has lower test error than the TF-IDF (1-2 gram) + logistic regression comparator on the 7,600 official test articles; on a held-out 10% split of train.csv it reached 7.75% error against 8.87% for the comparator.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 100 epochs beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0134, 95% CI [-0.0175, -0.0092], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 100 epochs with crop/flip augmentation, label smoothing, a one-cycle schedule and flip test-time augmentation reaches 4.78% error on a 5k held-out split of the CIFAR-10 training set when trained on 45k images, below the 6% reference; the same recipe trained on all 50k images produces the weights used for the hidden test predictions.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before choosing a problem, so I'll read the guide and the data READMEs first.
The guide's example was truncated, and I need the baseline script to know what "beating the comparator" means on CIFAR-10. I'll read both, plus the schema and the datasets list.

The baseline is 6% error on CIFAR-10, and the starter CNN is weak. I'll write a ResNet-9-style network with GPU-side crop and flip augmentation, label smoothing and a one-cycle schedule. Mode `val` trains on 45k and reports held-out error. Mode `full` trains on all 50k and saves weights. Mode `predict` loads those weights and writes predictions for the evaluator's inputs.
Run the same network for 50 epochs on the 45k/5k split to see whether more training moves validation error meaningfully.
Locate the work directory, patch run.py to take epochs as argv[2], then run the 50-epoch validation from there.
Run full-data training with 50 epochs and check which blob holds model.pt, since I need its id for `test.inputs` and `--input`.
List recorded runs to get the 50-epoch validation exec id. Then patch `predict` to fall back to a train slice when `EVAL_DIR` is unset, and smoke-test it with the saved weights.
Look up the validation exec id and the predict code hash in `lab runs`, then read the test-field part of the schema so the contribution is well-formed.
Print the `Test` and `Rel` definitions from the schema so the contribution uses the right keys.
Store the code directory as a blob, write the finding JSON, and submit it. The claim cites the 50-epoch validation exec and the test uses the full-data weights blob.
Run `lab put` with full output visible to find the blob id, then resubmit with the correct id.
Resubmit with the correct blob id, and make the statement match what the evidence measured.
Look for cached pretrained models and read the message board before deciding whether to spend the remaining time on AG News.

Write a single script with a `val` mode (train on 36k, score on a 4k split of train.csv, compare the comparator against word+char TF-IDF with LinearSVC and LR) and a `predict` mode (train on all 40k, write predictions for the hidden test set). Run `val` first.
Extend the C grid to 3 and 10 and rerun validation. If the trend holds, I'll use the best C for the predict run.
Run `predict` with C=1.0 to get the hidden-test predictions, store `ag/` with `lab put`, and list the runs so I can cite the validation exec.
Patch `predict` to fall back to a small training slice when `EVAL_DIR` is unset, smoke-test it, then store the patched code and read its blob id.
Write the AG News finding with both quantities from `exec-15e3a910`, then check its live status.

Build a fake `$EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv` from 50 training rows and run `predict 1.0` locally, pointing `OUT_DIR` at a temp folder. This checks that the EVAL branch reads the columns the test will provide.
Run the 100-epoch validation (about 5 minutes, under the 900s block limit). If it clearly beats 5.32%, I'll retrain the full model with 100 epochs and submit a new finding.
Run `full 100` to get weights for the test, then read the exec id and weights blob from the output.

Submit the 100-epoch CIFAR finding with the validation exec as evidence, the new weights as test input, and the predict code blob. The claim names the 45k-trained validation split and states that the test model is the same recipe on 50k.

Fetch the full-data weights blob, build a mock `$EVAL_DIR/cifar10/inputs.npz` with `x` and `id` from the training set, and run `predict` with `EVAL_DIR`, `IN_DIR` and `OUT_DIR` set. Then confirm the CSV has the right shape and columns.

List the artifacts to confirm which contributions are live, then end my part. The earlier `findin-9713d7a3` failed its live checks because of the bad code blob, so I'll note it as broken rather than rely on it.
Three findings are live and one (`findin-9713d7a3`) is broken from the bad code blob, so I'll leave it unpublished in my summary. Nothing else needs more compute, so I'll end my part.
